title: SOV Word Order and the Enclitic Copula
subtitle: Master the core Persian sentence structure and the present forms of 'to be'
keyPoint: Persian typically places the verb at the very end of the sentence (Subject-Object-Verb), and the present copula 'to be' attaches to adjectives or nouns.

examples.en: من دانشجو هستم.
او معلم خوب است.
ما در خانه هستیم.
شما بسیار مهربان هستید.
کتاب روی میز است.

mistakes.note: Verbs must go at the end of the clause in standard Persian word order.
The copula must agree with the subject plural marker (هستیم for ما).
Place complements appear before the copula, which remains in final position.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb to complete: 'I am a student' -> من دانشجو ___.
quiz.explanation: The first-person singular 'من' takes the ending '-am', giving 'هستم'.

quiz.question: Which sentence follows correct Persian SOV order for 'He is at home'?
quiz.explanation: Standard order requires Subject (او) + Prepositional Phrase (در خانه) + Verb (است).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'We are happy' -> ما خوشحال ___.
quiz.explanation: 'ما' (we) requires the first-person plural verb ending '-im', yielding 'هستیم'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'You (singular informal) are kind' -> تو مهربان ___.
quiz.explanation: 'تو' takes the second-person singular ending '-i', producing 'هستی'.

tip: In everyday speech, 'است' (ast) is often pronounced as a simple enclitic '-e' attached to the preceding consonant.

title: The Ezafe Construction (-e / -ye)
subtitle: Connecting nouns to adjectives and possessors
keyPoint: Ezafe is an unstressed vocalic bridge (-e after consonants, -ye after vowels) that links a head noun to its modifier or possessor.

examples.en: کتابِ جالب روی میز است.
خانهٔ علی بسیار زیبا است.
ماشینِ سفید متعلق به من است.
صدایِ باران آرامش‌بخش است.
کیفِ دستی نو خریدم.

mistakes.note: Adjectives modifying a noun must immediately follow it via Ezafe, not float after the verb.
Do not write double kasre marks; nouns ending in silent -eh or vowels take 'ی' or a solitary hamza mark.

mistakes.wrong: کتاب من نو است بدون کسره.
mistakes.note: Even when unwritten in informal text, the Ezafe sound must be pronounced when reading aloud.

quiz.question: Which phrase correctly expresses 'the big house' (خانه + بزرگ)?
quiz.explanation: Because 'خانه' ends in silent 'h' (pronounced 'e'), it requires the '-ye' Ezafe bridge, often marked with a small yeh/hamza (خانهٔ).

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'Ali's book'.
quiz.explanation: The head noun (کتاب) comes first, followed by the Ezafe sound (-e) and the possessor (علی).

quiz.question: Which connector sound is used after words ending in consonants like 'دست' (dast)?
quiz.explanation: Consonant-ending stems take the short unstressed vowel sound '-e' (kasre).

quiz.question: Which combination correctly means 'good student'?
quiz.explanation: Since 'دانشجو' ends with the vowel '-u', the bridge is written and pronounced with 'ی' (ye).

tip: Standard Persian writing often omits the short vowel mark (kasre), so you must supply the -e sound mentally based on syntax.

title: Simple Present Tense with the 'mi-' Prefix
subtitle: Conjugate ongoing and habitual present actions
keyPoint: The Persian present tense combines the prefix 'می-' (mi-) with the present stem and personal subject endings.

examples.en: من هر روز کتاب می‌خوانم.
او به دانشگاه می‌رود.
ما در رستوران غذا می‌خوریم.
شما نامه می‌نویسید.
آن‌ها فارسی صحبت می‌کنند.

mistakes.note: Dropping 'می-' alters the mood to subjunctive instead of indicative present tense.
Singular third person 'او' requires the ending '-ad' (می‌رود), not plural '-and'.
Standard orthography uses a zero-width non-joiner (half space) between 'میـ' and the stem.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'We write' -> ما نامه ___.
quiz.explanation: The subject 'ما' takes the first-person plural ending '-im' -> 'می‌نویسیم'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'I eat breakfast' -> من صبحانه ___.
quiz.explanation: Subject 'من' matches with suffix '-am' -> 'می‌خورم'.

quiz.question: What is the role of 'میـ' in the simple present tense?
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'میـ' (mi-) denotes indicative habitual or ongoing present aspect.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'They go' -> آن‌ها ___.
quiz.explanation: 'آن‌ها' is third-person plural, requiring '-and' -> 'می‌روند'.

tip: Present stems are historically irregular; memorize each verb's present stem alongside its infinitive.

title: Simple Past Tense Formation
subtitle: Build past actions by pruning the infinitive
keyPoint: Drop the final '-an' (-ن) from any infinitive to get the past stem, then add past personal endings (with zero ending for 3rd person singular).

examples.en: دیروز به سینما رفتم.
او ناهار را خورد.
ما در پارک قدم زدیم.
شما دیروز آمدید.
آن‌ها کتاب خواندند.

mistakes.note: The third-person singular past takes zero ending (no '-ad' like in the present).
Use the simple past stem of the verb itself rather than creating a superfluous compound verb.
Plural subjects take the past plural ending '-and'.

quiz.question: What is the past stem of 'نوشتن' (neveshtan - to write)?
quiz.explanation: Drop the final '-an' (-ن) from 'نوشتن' to yield the past stem 'نوشت'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct past form for 'He/She bought' (خریدن).
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular past tense has no ending; it is identical to the past stem 'خرید'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'We went home' -> ما به خانه ___.
quiz.explanation: Subject 'ما' pairs with the 1st person plural ending '-im' -> 'رفتیم'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'You (singular) saw the teacher' -> تو معلم را ___.
quiz.explanation: Subject 'تو' pairs with the 2nd person singular suffix '-i' -> 'دیدی'.

tip: Unlike present stems, every Persian verb has a 100% regular past stem derived simply by lopping off final '-an'.

title: Definite Direct Object Marker 'râ' (ro)
subtitle: Mark definite specific direct objects with precision
keyPoint: The postposition 'را' (râ) is placed immediately after a direct object when that object is definite or specifically identified.

cells: I read a book / read books

examples.en: من کتاب را خواندم.
دیروز مریم را در دانشگاه دیدم.
این ماشین را دوست دارم.
او کلید را پیدا کرد.
آن نامه را برای من بفرستید.

mistakes.note: Direct objects marked by 'را' stay before the final verb in Persian word order.
'را' is a postposition; it must follow the noun, never precede it.

mistakes.wrong: من یک سیب را خوردم (when non-specific).
mistakes.note: Indefinite non-specific direct objects should not take 'را'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I saw the car'?
quiz.explanation: 'ماشین' takes the postposition 'را' directly after it, and the verb stays at the end.

quiz.question: Why does 'علی را دیدم' require 'را'?
options: Because proper nouns are inherently definite direct objects
Because it is an indirect preposition
Because the verb is past tense
quiz.explanation: Proper names referring to the direct recipient of an action are inherently specific and definite.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'We bought this house' -> ما این خانه ___ خریدیم.
quiz.explanation: 'این خانه' is definite due to the demonstrative 'این', requiring the direct object marker 'را'.

quiz.question: Where does 'را' attach when a noun has an adjective, like 'کتابِ بزرگ' (the big book)?
quiz.explanation: 'را' marks the entire noun phrase and must be placed after the final modifier.

tip: In conversational Tehrani Persian, 'را' is routinely pronounced and written informally as 'رو' (ro) after vowels and 'و' (o) after consonants.

title: Pronominal Enclitics
subtitle: Attached personal endings for possession and objects
keyPoint: Pronominal enclitics attach directly to nouns, prepositions, or verbs to express possession or objects without using independent personal pronouns.

useCases.label: Complements of Prepositions
useCases.example: او با من صحبت کرد و ازم تشکر نمود.

useCases.label: Direct or Indirect Object
useCases.example: دیدمش و به او سلام کردم.

examples.en: کیفم را روی میز جا گذاشتم.
نامت را در لیست پیدا نکردم.
استاد صدایش را شنید.
خانه‌مان نزدیک ایستگاه مترو است.
دوستانشان دیروز به تهران رسیدند.

mistakes.note: Do not attach the enclitic to independent pronouns; attach it directly to the noun stem.
When a word ends in a silent 'eh' (ه), use a connecting hamzeh or keep a semi-space before adding the enclitic.

mistakes.wrong: ماشین من خراب است و ماشینم کار نمی‌کند
mistakes.note: Avoid using both the independent pronoun with ezafe ('ماشینِ من') and the pronominal enclitic ('ماشینم') simultaneously for the same noun.

quiz.question: How do you say 'my brother' using an enclitic?
quiz.explanation: The suffix for first-person singular possession is '-am' (ـَم), producing 'برادرم'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence to mean 'Where is your (singular) house?': '___ کجاست؟'
quiz.explanation: The second-person singular enclitic is '-at' (ـَت), giving 'خانه‌ات'.

quiz.question: Identify the word meaning 'their car':
quiz.explanation: The third-person plural enclitic is '-eshān' (ـِشان), giving 'ماشینشان'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct complement meaning 'I saw him/her': 'دیروز در دانشگاه ___.'
quiz.explanation: The third-person singular object enclitic '-ash' attaches to the conjugated past verb: 'دیدم' + 'ـَش' = 'دیدمش'.

tip: If a word ends in a long vowel like 'ā' (ا) or 'u' (و), insert an epenthetic 'y' (ی) before the singular enclitics (e.g., پا -> پایم).

title: Compound Verbs
subtitle: Combining nouns and adjectives with auxiliary light verbs
keyPoint: Persian compound verbs pair a non-verbal element with a light verb, where only the auxiliary verb conjugates for tense and person while the non-verbal base remains unchanged.

useCases.label: Active Operations with کردن
useCases.example: من هر روز در این شرکت کار می‌کنم.

useCases.label: Idiomatic Verbal Actions with زدن & دادن
useCases.example: علی با دوستانش در کافه حرف می‌زند.

examples.en: دانشجویان به سخنان استاد گوش دادند.
مادرم شام خوشمزه‌ای درست می‌کند.
پدرم تلویزیون را خاموش کرد.
ما درباره این موضوع با هم صحبت کردیم.
کلید گمشده بعد از دو روز پیدا شد.

mistakes.note: Prefixes like 'mi-' and 'be-' attach directly to the verbal element, never to the non-verbal noun or adjective.
Persian rarely invents simple verbs; conjugate the light verb 'کردن' instead of modifying the noun.
The negative prefix 'ne-' must precede the light verb stem, keeping the noun base intact.

quiz.question: Which verb correctly completes: 'او هر روز ورزش ___.' (He exercises every day)?
quiz.explanation: 'ورزش کردن' is the fixed compound verb meaning 'to exercise'.

quiz.question: Where does the continuous prefix 'mi-' go in 'زندگی کردن' for 'we live'?
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'میـ' attaches to the present stem of the light verb: 'زندگی می‌کنیم'.

quiz.question: Choose the compound verb that means 'to speak':
quiz.explanation: 'حرف زدن' pairs the noun 'حرف' with the light verb 'زدن' to mean 'to talk/speak'.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate 'تمیز کردن' (to clean) in past tense for 'they cleaned'?
quiz.explanation: The third-person plural past of 'کردن' is 'کردند', producing 'تمیز کردند'.

tip: Direct object markers (را) and prepositional phrases normally sit right before the light verb or before the entire compound verb, but prefixes like 'میـ' always attach directly to the verb stem.

title: Present Subjunctive
subtitle: Forming subjunctive verbs with the modal prefix be-
keyPoint: The present subjunctive is formed by adding the prefix 'be-' to the present verb stem along with personal endings to express wishes, doubts, or requests.

useCases.label: Uncertainty or Possibility with شاید
useCases.example: شاید او امروز به دانشگاه بیاید.

examples.en: امیدوارم فردا باران ببارد.
باید این نامه مهم را بنویسی.
می‌خواهم پنجره اتاق را باز کنم.
بهتر است حقیقت را بداند.
شاید فردا با دوستانم به سینما برویم.

mistakes.note: Verbs dependent on 'خواستن' take the subjunctive prefix 'بـ', not the indicative prefix 'میـ'.
Negating the modal or subjunctive verb takes 'نـ', replacing 'بـ' entirely (e.g., 'ننویسید', never 'بننویسید').
In many common compound verbs, the prefix 'بـ' is frequently dropped from the light verb.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'می‌خواهم به خانه ___.' (I want to go home)
quiz.explanation: The present subjunctive first-person singular of 'رفتن' is 'بروم' (prefix 'be-' + stem 'rav' + ending '-am').

quiz.question: What happens to the 'be-' prefix when a subjunctive verb is negated?
quiz.explanation: The negative marker 'نـ' replaces 'بـ' entirely (e.g., 'برود' becomes 'نرود').

quiz.question: Select the correct subjunctive form for 'you (singular) write':
quiz.explanation: 'بنویسی' consists of 'بـ' + present stem 'نویس' + 2nd singular personal ending 'ـی'.

quiz.question: Complete the obligation clause: 'باید آب سالم ___.' (We must drink healthy water)
quiz.explanation: 'باید' governs the subjunctive; for 'ما' the form is 'بنوشیم' (stem 'nush' + ending '-im').

tip: The vowel sound in the prefix 'بـ' harmonizes with the root vowel: it sounds like 'bo-' before stems containing 'o' or 'u' (e.g., 'بخور' - bokhor), and 'be-' elsewhere.

title: Modal Constructions
subtitle: Expressing necessity, possibility, and ability
keyPoint: Impersonal modals like 'باید' (must) and 'شاید' (might) stay invariable, whereas 'توانستن' (can) conjugates for person and tense; all require a subjunctive main verb.

useCases.label: Expressing Obligation (باید)
useCases.example: شما باید درس‌هایتان را مرور کنید.

useCases.label: Expressing Ability (توانستن)
useCases.example: آیا می‌توانی به زبان فارسی صحبت کنی؟

useCases.label: Expressing Speculation (شاید)
useCases.example: شاید فردا باران بیاید و هوا سرد شود.

examples.en: باید هر روز ورزش کنیم.
او می‌تواند پیانو بنوازد.
شاید هفته آینده به سفر بروند.
نتوانستم دیروز با شما تماس بگیرم.
باید حقیقت را به مادرت بگویی.

mistakes.note: 'باید' is an impersonal modal particle and never takes personal endings like '-am' in standard Persian.
The secondary verb following 'توانستن' must be in the present subjunctive, not a shortened infinitive.
Uncertain speculation with 'شاید' requires the present subjunctive rather than the indicative.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate 'باید' for the pronoun 'ما' (we)?
quiz.explanation: 'باید' is invariable and remains identical for all subjects.

quiz.question: Choose the sentence meaning 'I cannot come today':
quiz.explanation: 'نمی‌توانم' governs the 1st singular present subjunctive verb 'بیایم'.

quiz.question: Which modal is invariable and conveys uncertainty ('perhaps / maybe')?
quiz.explanation: 'شاید' is an invariable modal particle expressing probability or speculation.

quiz.question: Select the correct combination for 'You (formal) can help': 'شما می‌توانید ___.'
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary 'می‌توانید' governs the subjunctive form 'کمک کنید'.

tip: To negate obligation ('must not'), prefix 'na-' directly to the modal: 'نباید' (nabāyad), followed still by a subjunctive verb.

title: Past Continuous Tense
subtitle: Describing habitual and ongoing actions in the past
keyPoint: The past continuous is formed by attaching the imperfective prefix 'mi-' to the simple past stem along with past personal endings.

cells: I used to go / was going
you used to write / were writing
he/she used to read / was reading
we used to see / were seeing
they used to say / were saying

useCases.label: Habitual Past Behavior
useCases.example: وقتی کودک بودم، هر روز در کوچه بازی می‌کردم.

useCases.label: Ongoing Interrupted Action
useCases.example: داشتم کتاب می‌خواندم که علی آمد.

useCases.label: Past State over Time
useCases.example: آن زمان در شیراز زندگی می‌کردیم.

examples.en: هر روز صبح پیاده به مدرسه می‌رفتم.
وقتی تلفن زنگ زد، غذا می‌خوردیم.
او همیشه به دیگران کمک می‌کرد.
آن‌ها در آن سال‌ها سخت کار می‌کردند.
باران تندی در جنگل می‌بارید.

mistakes.note: Do not confuse the present stem with the past stem; 'mi-' attached to a present stem creates present tense, while 'mi-' with a past stem forms the past continuous.
The negative marker replaces or prefixes 'mi-' as 'نمیـ' (e.g., 'نمی‌خواندم'), never combining with 'be-'.
Do not add auxiliary 'بودم' to form the standard past continuous; the prefix 'میـ' alone marks the imperfective aspect.

quiz.question: Which verb form represents 'I used to eat / was eating'?
quiz.explanation: 'می‌خوردم' uses 'mi-' with the past stem 'خورد-' plus the first-person suffix '-am'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'they used to live' using 'زندگی کردن'?
quiz.explanation: The past continuous is formed on the past stem of the light verb: 'زندگی می‌کردند'.

quiz.question: Identify the tense of: 'شب‌ها داستان می‌نوشت.'
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'میـ' attached to the past 3rd-person singular stem 'نوشت' marks the past continuous.

quiz.question: Complete the negative sentence: 'ما در آن رودخانه شنا ___.' (We were not swimming)
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person plural negative past continuous of 'شنا کردن' is 'شنا نمی‌کردیم'.

tip: Persian past continuous serves as both 'used to [verb]' (habitual past) and 'was [verb]-ing' (progressive past). Context clarifies which English nuance applies.

title: Colloquial vs. Formal Persian Shifts
subtitle: Master common Tehrani spoken sound changes and grammatical reductions
keyPoint: Spoken Tehrani systematically transforms '-ân' into '-un', contracts the direct object marker 'râ' to 'ro' or 'o', and simplifies verb endings.

examples.en: من هر روز نون تازه می‌خرم.
این کلید رو به سارا بده.
او به خیابون رفت.
حالت چطوره؟
داری کجا میری؟

mistakes.note: Mixing formal 'نان' with colloquial 'رو' sounds inconsistent; spoken Persian shifts both simultaneously to 'نون رو'.
In natural spoken Persian, pronominal clitics (-esh / -esho) are preferred over full independent pronouns with 'رو'.
In speech, the subject pronoun 'او' shifts to 'اون' and the copula 'است' reduces to enclitic '-e'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'bread' in casual spoken Tehrani Persian?
quiz.explanation: The sequence 'ân' before nasal consonants almost universally shifts to 'un' in colloquial Persian.

quiz.question: Choose the colloquial equivalent for: 'او کتاب را خواند.'
quiz.explanation: 'او' becomes 'اون', 'را' becomes 'رو', and the vowel in 'خواند' shifts to 'خوند'.

quiz.question: What is the natural spoken reduction of 'خانه است' (It is a house)?
quiz.explanation: 'خانه' becomes 'خونه' and followed by the copula '-ast' contracts smoothly to 'خونه‌ست'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly reflects natural spoken direct object marking after a consonant?
quiz.explanation: After a consonant like 'ن', the colloquial object marker 'ro' often reduces simply to the enclitic 'o' (ماشینو).

tip: Spoken sound shifts like ân → un apply primarily to native Iranian roots (like نان → نون and باران → بارون), but rarely to formal Arabic loanwords (like قرآن or انقلاب).

title: The Indefinite Suffix '-i' (یای نکره)
subtitle: Mark non-specific reference with the unstressed suffix 'ی'
keyPoint: Attaching the unstressed suffix '-i' (ی) to a noun marks it as an indefinite entity ('a/an/a certain'), often reinforced by the numeral 'yek'.

examples.en: مردی در خیابان منتظر بود.
یک روزی به ایران سفر خواهم کرد.
من داستانی جالب خواندم.
او نامه‌ای برای من فرستاد.
سیبی از درخت افتاد.

mistakes.note: Do not combine the indefinite suffix '-i' with the specific definite marker 'râ' (را) unless specified by a restrictive relative clause.
Using bare 'yek' without '-i' often emphasizes the exact numeral 'one' rather than simple indefinite 'a/an'.
When a noun ends in silent 'h' (ه), the indefinite suffix requires an orthographic hamza/alef seat: 'نامه‌ای'.

quiz.question: Which word contains the indefinite suffix (یای نکره) meaning 'a child'?
quiz.explanation: 'کودکی' attaches unstressed '-i' to 'کودک' meaning 'a child'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I read an interesting book'?
options: من یک کتاب جالب را خواندم.
quiz.explanation: When an adjective follows an indefinite noun, the indefinite suffix '-i' attaches to the adjective: 'کتاب جالبی'.

quiz.question: Where does the indefinite suffix attach in the phrase 'یک سیب قرمز' (a red apple)?
quiz.explanation: The indefinite suffix attaches to the end of the entire noun phrase: 'یک سیب قرمزی'.

quiz.question: What is the difference between 'سیب خوردم' and 'سیبی خوردم'?
options: 'سیب' is past tense, 'سیبی' is present tense
'سیب خوردم' is generic (apple-eating), 'سیبی خوردم' means 'I ate an apple'
quiz.explanation: Bare nouns denote generic categories, while suffixing '-i' isolates a singular individual indefinite item.

tip: The indefinite suffix '-i' is always UNSTRESSED. If you pronounce the final '-i' with stress, it sounds like an abstract noun (e.g., مردی mardí = chivalry vs márdi = a man).

title: Past Participle, Pluperfect & Past Subjunctive
subtitle: Form compound past moods using the past participle with būdan
keyPoint: Combine the past participle (past stem + -e) with 'بودم' for the pluperfect, or with 'باشم' for the past subjunctive.

examples.en: قبل از رفتن، غذا خورده بودم.
شاید علی به دانشگاه رفته باشد.
باید تا دیروز کار را تمام کرده بودید.
امیدوارم قطار راه نیفتاده باشد.
ما قبلاً این فیلم را دیده بودیم.

mistakes.note: Expressions of uncertainty or hope regarding past events require the past subjunctive ('آمده باشد'), not simple past.
The present perfect uses enclitic copulas (-am, -i, -ast), not the free-standing verb 'هستم'.

mistakes.wrong: او کار را نکرده بود باشد.
mistakes.note: Past subjunctive is formed with 'باش-', never by stacking both 'بود' and 'باش'.

quiz.question: How do you complete the past perfect: 'من قبلاً او را ___' (I had seen him)?
quiz.explanation: The pluperfect (past perfect) is formed by the past participle + past of 'بودن' ('دیده بودم').

quiz.question: Choose the past subjunctive form for 'he might have gone': 'شاید او ___'
quiz.explanation: 'شاید' (perhaps) triggers the subjunctive; for past reference, use past participle + 'باشد'.

quiz.question: What is the past participle of 'نوشتن' (to write)?
quiz.explanation: Add the silent 'e' (ه) to the past stem (نوشت) to form 'نوشته'.

quiz.question: Select the correct sentence meaning 'They had already eaten':
quiz.explanation: 'آن‌ها خورده بودند' correctly conjugates the pluperfect for 3rd person plural.

tip: To spot the difference instantly: pluperfect ends in 'بود-' and expresses a completed past fact; past subjunctive ends in 'باش-' and expresses past doubt, obligation, or possibility.

title: Progressive Aspect with 'dâshtan'
subtitle: Express ongoing, uninterrupted actions in the present and past
keyPoint: Persian creates an explicit progressive tense by conjugating 'داشتن' right before a conjugated main verb that already carries 'می‌-'.

useCases.label: Interrupted Past Action
useCases.example: داشتم کتاب می‌خواندم که تلفن زنگ زد.

useCases.label: Strictly Ongoing State
useCases.example: بچه‌ها دارند در حیاط بازی می‌کنند.

examples.en: علی دارد تکالیفش را انجام می‌دهد.
ما داشتیم فیلم تماشا می‌کردیم.
داری چه کار می‌کنی؟
باران داشت به شدت می‌بارید.
آن‌ها دارند به سمت خانه می‌روند.

mistakes.note: Both auxiliary and main verb must match tense and person: 'دارم' (present) requires 'می‌خورم' (present).
The auxiliary 'داشتن' is never negated for progressive meaning; simply negate the standard continuous verb ('نمی‌روم').
The main verb MUST retain the prefix 'می‌-' when preceded by 'داشتن'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'وقتی رسیدی، من ___ غذا می‌پختم.'
quiz.explanation: Matching the past progressive 'می‌پختم' requires the 1st person singular past auxiliary 'داشتم'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'We are currently speaking' in Persian?
quiz.explanation: Present progressive for 'ما' is 'داریم' + present continuous 'صحبت می‌کنیم'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly demonstrates the progressive aspect?
options: سارا دارد به موسیقی گوش می‌دهد.
سارا داشت به موسیقی گوش داد.
quiz.explanation: 'دارد' matches the present continuous main verb 'گوش می‌دهد'.

quiz.question: Can the progressive auxiliary 'داشتن' be negated (e.g., ندارم می‌روم)?
options: Yes, it is common in formal Persian.
Yes, but only in past tense.
No, Persian negates the main continuous verb directly without داشتن.
quiz.explanation: Persian does not use 'داشتن' in the negative; you simply use the standard negative imperfective (e.g. 'نمی‌روم').

tip: Remember: both the auxiliary 'داشتن' and the main verb must agree in person and tense (e.g., 'داشتم می‌رفتم' — both 1st person singular past).

title: Passive Voice with 'shodan'
subtitle: Convert transitive verbs into the passive using past participle + shodan
keyPoint: The passive voice is formed by taking the past participle of a transitive verb and adding a conjugated form of 'شدن'.

useCases.label: Simple Verb Passive
useCases.example: این کتاب در سال گذشته نوشته شد.

examples.en: نامه دیروز فرستاده شد.
درهای دانشگاه بسته شدند.
این خانه سال گذشته ساخته شد.
غذا در آشپزخانه آماده می‌شود.
رمز عبور تغییر داده شد.

mistakes.note: Compound verbs with 'کردن' form the passive by replacing 'کردن' with 'شدن', not keeping 'کرد'.
Persian uses 'شدن' as the passive auxiliary, never 'آمدن'.
In standard Persian, plural animate and prominent subjects in passive clauses require plural verb agreement ('شدند').

quiz.question: How do you say 'The door was opened'?
quiz.explanation: The compound verb 'باز کردن' forms its simple past passive by replacing 'کرد' with 'شد'.

quiz.question: What is the passive form of 'نوشت' (he/she wrote)?
quiz.explanation: Past stem 'نوشت' + -e = 'نوشته', followed by 'شد' = 'نوشته شد'.

quiz.question: Change into the present passive: 'او پنجره را می‌شکند.' (The window is broken...)
quiz.explanation: Present continuous passive uses the past participle + 'می‌شود': 'شکسته می‌شود'.

quiz.question: How do compound verbs formed with 'کردن' generally form their passive?
quiz.explanation: Compound verbs with 'کردن' (like 'تعمیر کردن') simply swap 'کردن' for 'شدن' ('تعمیر شدن').

tip: For compound verbs formed with 'کردن' (like 'پیدا کردن' to find), simply substitute 'کردن' with 'شدن' ('پیدا شدن' to be found) without needing a past participle.

title: Morphological Causative Verbs (-ândan / -ânidan)
subtitle: Deriving transitive and causative verbs from present stems
keyPoint: Add the suffix -ândan (or -ânidan) to the present stem of an intransitive verb to create a regular transitive causative verb.

useCases.label: Making Someone Do an Action
useCases.example: مادر کودک را سر سفره نشاند.

useCases.label: Causing a Psychological State
useCases.example: صدای رعد و برق بچه‌ها را ترساند.

useCases.label: Physical Transfer or Delivery
useCases.example: پستچی نامه را به دست من رساند.

examples.en: او همیشه برادر کوچکش را می‌ترساند.
پرستار بیمار را روی تخت خواباند.
راننده مسافران را به فرودگاه رساند.
باد برگ‌های پاییزی را رقصاند.
معلم دانش‌آموز را سر جایش نشاند.

mistakes.note: Intransitive verbs like 'خوابیدن' cannot take a direct object ('را'); you must derive the causative form 'خواباندن'.
Do not construct artificial compound verbs with 'کردن' when a direct morphological causative with '-ândan' exists.

mistakes.wrong: او نامه را به ما رسید.
mistakes.right: او نامه را به ما رساند.
mistakes.note: 'رسیدن' means 'to arrive' (intransitive); use 'رساندن' to mean 'to deliver' or 'to cause to arrive'.

quiz.question: The thunder ___ the small children last night.
quiz.explanation: The causative form 'ترساند' is needed because the thunder caused the children to fear (direct object 'بچه‌ها را').

quiz.question: I ___ my friend to the train station on time.
quiz.explanation: 'رساندم' (first-person singular causative past) means 'I delivered / gave a lift to someone'.

quiz.question: The mother gently ___ the baby in the crib.
quiz.explanation: 'خواباند' is the transitive causative past of 'خوابیدن', meaning 'put to sleep'.

quiz.question: The teacher ___ all the students in the auditorium.
quiz.explanation: 'نشاند' is the transitive causative stem used for making someone sit down.

tip: All causative verbs formed with '-ândan' behave as completely regular verbs in both past and present (present stem ends in '-ân', e.g., می‌ترساند).

title: Restrictive Relative Clauses with 'ke' and Resumptive Pronouns
subtitle: Connecting clauses using the restrictive marker -i and resumptive enclitics
keyPoint: Attach the restrictive enclitic '-i' (ی) to the head noun before 'که' and retain an obligatory pronominal clitic inside the clause whenever the relativized noun serves as an object or prepositional complement.

cells: کتابی که آن را خریدم / دیروز خریدمش
مردی که با او / باهاش صحبت کردم
Clitic marks possession inside relative clause
No resumptive clitic needed for subject head

useCases.label: Restrictive Clause with Preposition
useCases.example: این همان خانه‌ای است که در آن بزرگ شدم.

useCases.label: Object Relative Clause with Clitic
useCases.example: فیلمی که دیشب دیدمش بسیار جالب بود.

useCases.label: Possessive Subordinate Reference
useCases.example: نویسنده‌ای که کتابش برنده شد اینجاست.

examples.en: مردی که دیروز با او حرف زدی وکیلم است.
کتابی که خریدمش روی میز است.
دانشجویی که نمره‌اش بیست شد جایزه گرفت.
ماشینی که موتورش خراب است حرکت نمی‌کند.
دوستی که به او اعتماد دارم امروز می‌آید.

mistakes.wrong: مرد که دیروز دیدم مهربان بود.
mistakes.right: مردی که دیروز دیدم مهربان بود.
mistakes.note: A restrictive relative clause requires the restrictive suffix '-i' (ی) attached to the head noun.

mistakes.wrong: دوستی که با صحبت کردم آمد.
mistakes.right: دوستی که با او صحبت کردم آمد.
mistakes.note: A preposition inside a relative clause cannot stand stranded without a resumptive pronoun object.
In standard formal syntax, the copula 'است' precedes the relative clause when defining the subject.

quiz.question: The student ___ car was stolen called the police.
quiz.explanation: The head noun must take the restrictive '-i' (دانشجویی), and 'ماشینش' contains the required resumptive clitic '-ash'.

quiz.question: This is the colleague ___ I traveled to Isfahan with.
options: همکاری که با او سفر کردم
همکار که با او سفر کرد
همکاری با او که سفر کردم
quiz.explanation: 'همکاری که' marks the restricted antecedent, followed by preposition + resumptive pronoun 'با او'.

quiz.question: The house ___ doors were painted blue looks beautiful.
quiz.explanation: The head noun takes '-i' (خانه‌ای) and the possessive relationship in the clause requires the clitic '-ash' on 'درهایش'.

quiz.question: The poem ___ I heard yesterday was profound.
quiz.explanation: 'شعری که' features the restrictive marker, while 'شنیدمش' appropriately retains the resumptive direct object clitic.

tip: Unlike English, which drops prepositions or moves them ('the man I spoke to'), Persian never strands prepositions; 'با', 'به', and 'از' must always attach to a resumptive pronoun like 'او' or an enclitic.

title: Hypothetical and Counterfactual Conditionals
subtitle: Expressing impossible past events and unreal present situations with agar
keyPoint: Counterfactual conditionals employ the past imperfective (می‌ + past stem) or past subjunctive in the condition clause and past imperfective in the result clause.

cells: I do not have time now, so I cannot come
Had he studied in the past, he would have passed
Past action with present hypothetical result
Subjunctive past in protasis expressing contrary to fact

useCases.label: Unreal Present Condition
useCases.example: اگر پول کافی داشتم، همین امروز آن خانه را می‌خریدم.

useCases.label: Regret over Past Action
useCases.example: اگر به هشدارهای پلیس گوش داده بودی، جریمه نمی‌شدی.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Counterfactual Scenario
useCases.example: اگر او حقیقت را می‌دانست، هرگز با آن‌ها همکاری نمی‌کرد.

examples.en: اگر دیروز هوا خوب بود، به کوه می‌رفتیم.
اگر به من گفته بودید، حتماً کمکتان می‌کردم.
اگر بال داشتم، به آسمان پرواز می‌کردم.
اگر کلید را فراموش نکرده بودم، پشت در نمی‌ماندم.
اگر پزشک اینجا بود، بیمار نجات پیدا می‌کرد.

mistakes.wrong: اگر پول داشته باشم، آن خانه را می‌خریدم.
mistakes.right: اگر پول داشتم، آن خانه را می‌خریدم.
mistakes.note: Do not mix the present subjunctive (داشته باشم - real future) with a counterfactual past apodosis (می‌خریدم).

mistakes.right: اگر دیروز باران باریده بود، نمی‌رفتیم.
mistakes.note: Counterfactual past events require the past perfect or past imperfective in Persian, not simple past indicative.

mistakes.wrong: اگر تو جای من بودی، چه کار کردی؟
mistakes.right: اگر تو جای من بودی، چه کار می‌کردی؟
mistakes.note: The apodosis (result clause) of an unreal conditional must have the continuous prefix 'می‌'.

quiz.question: If you had informed me earlier, I ___ you immediately.
quiz.explanation: Counterfactual result clauses require the past imperfective with 'می‌' ('کمکت می‌کردم').

quiz.question: If we had taken the train, we ___ late.
quiz.explanation: 'نمی‌رسیدیم' represents the past continuous negative used for unreal past results.

quiz.question: If she ___ the secret, she wouldn't have cried.
quiz.explanation: The past perfect subjunctive/indicative ('دانسته بود') correctly establishes the prior counterfactual condition.

quiz.question: If I were rich right now, I ___ around the world.
quiz.explanation: For an unreal present conditional, the result clause takes the past continuous ('سفر می‌کردم').

tip: Notice how the prefix 'می‌' on past stems functions like 'would' in English unreal conditionals (e.g., می‌رفتم = 'I would go' or 'I would have gone').

title: Short Infinitives and Deverbal Nominal Derivations
subtitle: Past stems as short infinitives and compound nominal stems
keyPoint: Dropping the final -an from full infinitives produces 'short infinitives' (past stems), which function as action nouns and combine with present stems to create abstract deverbal compounds.

useCases.label: Round-Trip and Reciprocal Actions
useCases.example: بلیط رفت و برگشت به شیراز بسیار گران شده است.

useCases.label: Abstract Deverbal Compounds
useCases.example: گفت‌وگو میان دو طرف ساعت‌ها به طول انجامید.

useCases.label: Short Infinitive as Object of Preposition
useCases.example: پس از رسیدن قطار، هنگام پیاده شدن مسافران شلوغ شد.

examples.en: خرید و فروش ملک در این منطقه سودآور است.
دانشمندان در حال جست‌وجو برای یافتن دارو هستند.
دید و بازدید عید یکی از سنت‌های کهن است.
هنگام شست‌وشو باید از آب سرد استفاده کرد.
رفت و آمد ماشین‌ها در مرکز شهر محدود شد.

mistakes.note: Idiomatic nominal compounds and tickets use truncated past stems ('رفت و برگشت'), not full long infinitives.

mistakes.wrong: آن‌ها در حال گفتن و شنیدن بودند.
mistakes.note: The standard abstract nominal for 'dialogue/negotiation' is the compound 'گفت‌وگو' (or گفت‌و‌شنود).

mistakes.wrong: برای خریدن این کتاب، جستن و جویدن زیادی کردم.
mistakes.right: برای خرید این کتاب، جست‌وجوی زیادی کردم.
mistakes.note: Use the nominalized stem compound 'جست‌وجو' rather than awkward full coordinated infinitives.

quiz.question: We bought a ___ train ticket to Mashhad.
quiz.explanation: 'رفت و برگشت' uses short infinitives (past stems) coupled with the conjunction 'o' to mean 'round trip'.

quiz.question: The diplomatic ___ lasted until midnight.
quiz.explanation: 'گفت‌وگو' combines past stem 'گفت' + present stem 'گو' to form the abstract noun 'conversation/dialogue'.

quiz.question: Commercial ___ has expanded rapidly in the capital.
quiz.explanation: 'خرید و فروش' (buying and selling / commerce) uses the short infinitive pairing formula.

quiz.question: Urban traffic (literally: coming and going) is dense today: ___ سنگین است.
quiz.explanation: 'رفت و آمد' is the standard compound noun for transit, traffic, and commuting.

tip: Short infinitives (like 'دید', 'شنید', 'خرید') are completely identical to the third-person singular simple past, but function syntactically as pure nouns.

title: Clitic Climbing and Syntactic Dislocation
subtitle: Managing pronominal enclitics and topicalized objects in complex predicates
keyPoint: In compound verbs and modal verb phrases, pronominal object enclitics can 'climb' from the main infinitive or verbal noun and attach to the non-verbal element or auxiliary.

useCases.label: Clitic Attachment to Non-Verbal Stem
useCases.example: فراموشش کردم چون دیگر اهمیتی نداشت.

useCases.label: Complex Object Dislocation (Topicalization)
useCases.example: این موضوع مهم را، سال‌ها پیش بررسی‌اش کرده بودیم.

useCases.label: Clitic on Prepositional Element in Compound
useCases.example: فرصت طلایی را خیلی ساده از دستش داد.

examples.en: کلیدم گم شده بود اما بالاخره پیدایش کردم.
این خاطره تلخ را هیچ‌وقت فراموشش نمی‌کنم.
بچه‌ها بازیگوش هستند، آرامشان کن.
اگر پیراهن کثیف است، تمیزش می‌کنم.
این داستان زیبا را بارها خواندمش.

mistakes.right: من پیدایش کردم. / من او را پیدا کردم.
mistakes.note: In natural Persian, pronominal direct objects are expressed either with pre-verbal 'او را' or enclitics on the nominal element ('پیدایش کردم').
In compound verbs formed with 'کردن', the object enclitic prefers to attach directly to the nominal part ('پیدایش'), not to the auxiliary verb ending.

mistakes.wrong: این کتاب را، من نخواندم آن.
mistakes.note: Topicalized definite objects marked with 'را' take a resumptive enclitic ('-ash' / '-esh') rather than an independent pronoun at the end.

quiz.question: I lost my sunglasses yesterday, but today I ___ under the sofa.
quiz.explanation: In 'پیدایش کردم', the 3rd person singular enclitic '-ash' attaches to the nominal base 'پیدا'.

quiz.question: That old house? We ___ two years ago.
quiz.explanation: 'خرابش کردیم' shows standard clitic climbing onto the adjective 'خراب' before the verbal light verb 'کردیم'.

quiz.question: The soup was completely cold, so she ___ in the microwave.
quiz.explanation: 'گرمش کرد' (she warmed it up) correctly positions the clitic '-ash' on the adjective 'گرم'.

quiz.question: As for this antique Persian rug, my grandfather ___ fifty years ago.
quiz.explanation: 'خریدش' attaches the resumptive enclitic '-ash' directly to the transitive simple verb.

tip: In everyday formal and colloquial Persian compound verbs (Noun + کردن/زدن/دادن), the enclitic pronoun (-am, -at, -ash) almost always attaches to the NOUN, not to the auxiliary verb.
